title: From apprentice electrician to electrical contractor, the career ladder explained with Ledger in 90 seconds
summary: A hands-on trade ladder, apprentice to the person who owns the firm and the licence; fits Hoang's 'technician' and everyday-job direction.

beats.label: title
beats.voice: From apprentice electrician to electrical contractor, the career ladder explained with Ledger in ninety seconds.
onScreen: From apprentice electrician to electrical contractor, the career ladder explained with Ledger
beats.visual: Title scene: full-bleed room, a ladder on the right, the five steps below, small Ledger in the el_apprentice outfit waving on the bottom step; a dashed arrow climbs to the top; the title card and the 90-second pill appear on the title words

beats.label: rung 1 THE APPRENTICE
beats.voice: First, Ledger is the apprentice electrician, with a hard hat and a tool pouch.
beats.visual: OUTFIT (el_apprentice: yellow hard hat, hi-vis vest over a grey tee, tool pouch, lanyard). Header THE APPRENTICE. Ledger alone, scale 3.2, yellow hard hat; arrows pop in on 'hard hat' and 'tool pouch'

beats.label: rung 1 THE APPRENTICE
beats.voice: Then he pulls cable and fits sockets, under a journeyman's eye.
beats.visual: Cable runs along a wall and a socket clicks in; a small journeyman figure watches

beats.label: rung 1 THE APPRENTICE
beats.voice: He also learns the code, and safe habits.
beats.visual: A code book opens; a safety tick appears on a checklist

beats.label: rung 1 THE APPRENTICE
beats.voice: So on this rung, he installs under supervision.
beats.visual: Slider at 0.06 on 'Installs'; the journeyman's hand rests on his shoulder

beats.label: climb 1 to 2
beats.voice: After that, he climbs to journeyman.
beats.visual: Ledger climbs the ladder from rung 1 to rung 2; his outfit swaps mid-climb to the next set; the next rung tag lights up on the naming word

beats.label: rung 2 JOURNEYMAN
beats.voice: Now he is licensed, and works on his own.
beats.visual: OUTFIT (el_journeyman: blue work shirt with rolled sleeves, tool belt, voltage tester in pocket, no hard-hat strap). Header JOURNEYMAN. A licence card pops up beside Ledger; he walks into a house alone

beats.label: rung 2 JOURNEYMAN
beats.voice: Then he reads blueprints, and installs and repairs the wiring.
beats.visual: A blueprint unrolls; a lamp flickers and then stays on after his repair

beats.label: rung 2 JOURNEYMAN
beats.voice: And he teaches the apprentices, and tests each circuit.
beats.visual: A new apprentice figure copies his move; a tester shows a green light

beats.label: climb 2 to 3
beats.voice: Then he climbs again, to master electrician.
beats.visual: Ledger climbs the ladder from rung 2 to rung 3; his outfit swaps mid-climb to the next set; the next rung tag lights up on the naming word

beats.label: rung 3 THE MASTER
beats.voice: As master, he signs off the work, and pulls permits.
beats.visual: OUTFIT (el_master: charcoal work jacket, glasses, clipboard, a master badge on the chest). Header THE MASTER. A permit form gets a stamp; Ledger signs a job sheet

beats.label: rung 3 THE MASTER
beats.voice: Then he checks each job against the code, and leads the crew.
beats.visual: Three crew figures in a row; a code tick passes along them

beats.label: rung 3 THE MASTER
beats.voice: So he installs less, and starts to run jobs.
beats.visual: Slider at 0.35; a job board with three jobs behind him

beats.label: climb 3 to 4
beats.voice: Next, he steps up as project manager.
beats.visual: Ledger climbs the ladder from rung 3 to rung 4; his outfit swaps mid-climb to the next set; the next rung tag lights up on the naming word

beats.label: rung 4 PROJECT MANAGER
beats.voice: Now he plans each job, and estimates the cost.
beats.visual: OUTFIT (el_pm: white hard hat, tablet, grey fleece vest, site boots). Header PROJECT MANAGER. A quote sheet adds up line by line on a tablet

beats.label: rung 4 PROJECT MANAGER
beats.voice: Then he orders materials, and schedules the crews on site.
beats.visual: A materials delivery arrives; a crew calendar fills in colours

beats.label: climb 4 to 5
beats.voice: Finally, he reaches the top rung, as contractor owner.
beats.visual: Ledger climbs the ladder from rung 4 to rung 5; his outfit swaps mid-climb to the next set; the next rung tag lights up on the naming word

beats.label: rung 5 CONTRACTOR OWNER
beats.voice: As contractor, he owns the firm, and is legally responsible for the work.
beats.visual: OUTFIT (el_owner: black jacket with the company name on the chest, gold pocket square, glasses, grey temples). Header CONTRACTOR OWNER. A van with a company sign appears; a licence frame lights up

beats.label: rung 5 CONTRACTOR OWNER
beats.voice: He sets prices, and pays for tools, insurance and crews.
beats.visual: A price list; pots labelled tools, insurance, crews fill from coin pieces

beats.label: rung 5 CONTRACTOR OWNER
beats.voice: Yet he installs almost nothing himself, and answers for every job.
beats.visual: Slider at 0.95 on 'Runs'; every job on the board gets a tick

beats.label: payoff
beats.voice: So with each rung, Ledger installed less, and ran more.
beats.visual: Five Ledgers on the ladder, all five tags ticked, the slider runs from the bottom word to the top word

beats.label: cta
beats.voice: To climb your own career ladder, learn technical business concepts at Edlintics.

caption:
From apprentice electrician to contractor owner, the job changes on every rung

The apprentice pulls cable under supervision, and the journeyman works on his own and teaches the apprentices. Then the master electrician signs off the work and pulls the permits. Finally, the contractor owns the firm and answers for every job

So each rung up, you install less yourself and run more. Walk up the ladder with Ledger and note which rung you are on

sources.claim: Electrician path: 4 to 5 year apprenticeship, journeyworker duties (blueprints, wiring, troubleshooting), master electrician, supervisor or project management roles; about 7 percent self-employed
Electrician duties, apprenticeship, site supervision, estimating and contract management, and setting up your own electrical business
Apprentice, journeyman, master electrician levels; master can pull permits; contractors are legally responsible for the workers and the work (it does not cover owning a business)

openQuestions: Rung 4 'project manager' is from the BLS (supervisor or project management roles) and the National Careers Service (site supervision, estimating, contract management); the rung is optional on some firms. Licence names vary by country (journeyman vs journeyworker, master electrician not offered in every state).

Top rung 'owns the firm' rests on BLS (7 percent self-employed) and National Careers Service (set up your own business); no source details contractor-owner duties, so the script keeps them to prices, pay and legal responsibility (Fluke). Flagged as the weakest rung.
Titles vary by employer and country; the caption says nothing about pay or years
